## 1. Panel design layer: theme variables, icons, mascot

The panel's look comes from three small modules. All are plain CommonJS; they need no build step and do not trip the CSP.

- **`vscode/theme.js` (THEME_CSS):** defines design variables on `body`:
  - `--acc`, by theme type: light `#c2410c`, dark `#fb923c`, high contrast `#ffa94d` / `#9a3412`.
  - `--acc-ink` (text on the accent), `--acc-soft`, `--acc-line`.
  - `--surface`, `--surface-2`, `--line`, `--muted`, `--shadow` (none in high contrast).
  - `--r-*` corners, `--fs-*` type scale.

  The same file has the app bar styles: mascot, repo chip, tabs with icons, search box, Audit/Scan buttons. The app bar is sticky; below 760px it is not sticky. Its height is written as `--appbar-h`, and the Tasks list and the Contents panel stick under it.
- **`vscode/icons.js`:** Lucide icons (ISC license). Not edited by hand; `npm run icons` (`scripts/icons.mjs`) generates only the ones in the NAMES list from `lucide-static`. `tasksView.icon(name, size)` draws them. The types in the Agent changes tab use these icons too.
- **`vscode/mascot.js`:** the mascot from `assets/logo.svg` is embedded inline (the gradient ids are prefixed with `imp-`). It is shown in the header and in empty screens (`.emptyhero`).

**Rules:**

- No fixed hex colors in the Tasks CSS (a test checks this).
- Secondary text is written with the `--muted` color, not with opacity.
- Mermaid diagrams are drawn with `theme: base`; their colors are computed from the page's `--vscode-editor-background`, `--vscode-foreground` and `--acc` values.

vscode-elements was deliberately not used; the reason is in the linked ADR.

### The board look (#148, 0.95.0)

On dark and light themes, `theme.js` defines board tokens (`--b-bg`, `--b-panel`, `--b-card` gradient, `--b-line`, `--b-text`, `--b-muted`). It points the `--vscode-*` colours the panel uses (editor background, foreground, description, borders, inputs, hover) and its own tokens (`--surface`, `--line`, `--muted`, `--shadow`, radii) at them. Every tab follows without component edits. Cards (`.card`, `.bucket`, `.etable`, `.tablewrap`) get the board gradient, and the app bar blurs. Muted text stays legible: #a3a19a on dark, #5f5d57 on light. High-contrast themes keep VS Code's colours.

### Decisions settled

- 6951: the panel's look is its own theme layer (a per-theme-type accent colour plus VS Code CSS variables) with Lucide icons, instead of adopting the vscode-elements component library.

## 2. Panel and views

### Editor and Markdown preview

- For every file that has a copy, the extension compares the file with the copy: the common head/tail is trimmed, then a line LCS, then a word LCS on the changed lines. If a single word changed it gets a word mark; if several words changed, the old sentence shows above the line as a CodeLens (the editor API cannot insert real lines). An added line is green, a deleted block is a red mark on the previous line.
- The preview gets a markdown-it plugin: the change is marked at block level, the old text is read in a red box above it, and notches like an overview ruler sit on the right edge (`preview-markers.js`).
- **Accept** works per Markdown unit (block boundaries come from VS Code's markdown-it): a CodeLens in the editor, a link above the block in the preview (`vscode://halilural.imprimatur/accept?…`, `registerUriHandler`). Accept writes only to the copy and never touches the file text; the view moves on to the next change.
- `imprimatur.showIn`: `preview` (default), `both`, `editor`; `imprimatur.editorAlsoFor` globs. No marks are drawn in diff tabs (Working Tree). The Mermaid diff is turned on with `imprimatur.mermaidDiff` (off by default).

### The Imprimatur panel (a single webview, `imprimatur.graph`)

Six tabs; only the visible tab's HTML is rendered:

| Tab | Source | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Home | `tasksView.js` | Progress, where each task left off, the first 5 items waiting on you, the task table |
| Tasks | `tasksView.js` | Task list by status (this repo or all repos); task page: 👉, waiting items and the answer box, todos, quick add (`?` question, `!` decision, `#` note, `@me` the user's todo), decisions, ADR, PDR, tests, activity |
| Waiting on you | `tasksView.js` + `waiting.js` | Everything waiting on the user, by task; end-of-turn requests as steps with checkboxes |
| Architecture / Product | `docsView.js` | Contents, rendered Markdown, contributing records, edit, mark superseded, section history |
| Agent changes | `graph.js` | The Agent Change Graph: one row per edit, a colored strip per task, the agent's other actions filtered by type |

The view builders are pure: they take a database connection and return a model or HTML; unit tests run without VS Code. The panel is usable by keyboard (j/k, Enter, x, a, /, Esc). What the user writes goes to the database with the actor `user`.

### Agent Change Graph

- Rows come from `history/**.jsonl`; the strip is the **task**, not the Claude session: the file under `docs/todos/<key>/`, the branch at the time of the edit (`<type>/<n>-name` → `#n`), the task of the records written in the same turn, the key in the request; otherwise "No task".
- Order of the description: the model's one sentence → the Bash description → the agent's words in the same message (`narration.js`) → the nearest heading + the first changed line.
- The hover opens only from the status cell; it shows a Markdown edit in the preview's review view. The right click is VS Code's own menu (Accept this edit, Open diff, Go to change).
- Performance: a per-file cache (size + mtime key), no word diff in the counts; on a real repository a full refresh went from 430 to 34 ms.

### Sidebar

The Imprimatur icon in the activity bar: rows that open the panel in a tab (the badge counts the items waiting on you) and the **Agent setup** tree: every file in the repo and in home that affects the agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, AGENTS.md, Gemini, Windsurf, Cline, Aider, git hooks), grouped by tool and type, with new/changed/deleted since the last look marked; when each one takes effect, health checks, drift between repos, git history and merged settings (hook order, effective permissions). It is read-only.

#### Decisions settled

- 580: the extension compares a file to its baseline copy with a line LCS and a word LCS, marking single-word changes at word level and multi-word changes at sentence level.
- 581: Accept works per Markdown unit, using VS Code's own markdown-it to find block boundaries, so a table or a run of added list items accepts as one group.
- 582: the preview carries overview-ruler-like marker notches on the right edge, one per marked block.
- 583: `imprimatur.showIn` controls where marks are drawn (preview by default, `both`, or `editor`); `imprimatur.editorAlsoFor` opts specific Markdown globs into editor marks too.
- 584: marks, CodeLenses, the status bar and the graph redraw themselves after review-data writes, debounced (0.5s/2s); the preview only reloads after copy/history changes or an Accept, not on every document edit.
- 585: no marks are drawn on either side of a diff tab (Working Tree, git compare).
- 586: the Mermaid diagram diff defaults off, because two other Mermaid preview extensions already compete for the same webview.
- 587: a numbered list's renumbering after a deletion is not treated as a change; only the deleted item is marked.
- 588: changes inside fenced code blocks are not marked, in the editor, the preview or the status bar count.
- 589: a changed sentence's old text shows above the line via a CodeLens, since the extension API cannot insert a real view-zone line in the editor.
- 590: there is one single view of an edit; the earlier "latest edit bright, older ones faded" distinction was removed because the faded box's opacity hid the Accept button.
- 591: a status-bar history button lists a file's agent edits like `git log`, each opened as a built-in `vscode.diff`.
- 592: the Agent Change Graph is a webview panel, laid out like Git Graph, built from `history/**.jsonl` across the repo.
- 593: the Agent Change Graph's description column follows this order: the model's one sentence → the Bash tool's own description → the agent's words in the same chat turn → the nearest heading plus the first changed line; it stopped being the user's own request text because short replies like "sure" were meaningless there.
- 594: a Graph lane is a task, not a Claude session, because one session can work on several different things.
- 595: the Graph's status column carries the Accept control; the hover popup opens only from the status cell (hovering elsewhere made the row hard to read), and the right-click menu is VS Code's own context menu.
- 596: Agent Setup lists every file that affects the agent, for the repo and for home, grouped by tool and kind, read-only.
- 597: the Waiting on you tab keeps every step's full history (open/done/replaced/answered/closed) rather than only the currently-open items, so a resolved question is not lost.
- 607: a mark disappears only with Accept or Accept all; staging, committing or reopening the file never touches it.
- 608: Accept in the preview updates instantly (removes the mark and the button client-side) instead of reloading the whole page.
- 613: hovering a Markdown edit in the Graph shows it rendered through the preview's own review view, not as a raw text diff.
- 616: if annotating a block throws, the preview falls back to drawing it unmarked rather than failing to render at all.
- 617: the preview gets its marks through a markdown-it plugin that annotates the already-cached token tree at render time, at block level.
- 618: editor marks are word/sentence level and preview marks are block level; this split, not full parity, is the accepted limit.
- 5577: the panel is one webview with tabs, each tab's view builder a pure function (db in, model/HTML out) so it is unit-testable without VS Code; the sidebar's narrow record trees were replaced by this because they were "unreadable".

## 3. Live updates

Goal: a change shows up in the panel the moment it is written. This is all local to the machine.

### Database file watcher

- `watch.js` watches the database file (and `-wal`, `-shm`) through its folder with `fs.watch`. **The first event is handled immediately**; while events continue, at most once every 50 ms, and once more at the end. If the watcher fails (folder deleted, watcher limit), it is set up again at most every 5 s.
- A single **change gate** (`PRAGMA data_version` + the extension's own transactions) is shared by the watcher, the backstop poll and the extension's own writes: a change is drawn once.
- While the panel is visible, the change stamp is checked every 500 ms (the backstop, in case the watcher misses an event). There is no polling while the panel is hidden.
- Measured: the file watcher takes 25 to 49 ms; the target is about 50 ms. An integration test checks that a record written from another process reaches the panel within 500 ms.

### Hook writes under `.claude/imprimatur/` (#114)

`refresh-route.js` `routeOf` decides what a write redraws:

- **edits** (`baseline/`, `history/`): the editors, lenses, preview and panel, once, 300 ms after the last write (at least every 2 s while writes keep coming). An open file also redraws when its text changes (`onDidChangeTextDocument`), so the late redraws of old are not needed.
- **graph** (`waiting/`, `activity/`, `descriptions.jsonl`, `calls.jsonl`, anything new): the panel and the counts, 1 s after the last write (at least every 3 s).
- **none** (`pending/`, `process.json`, `open-edits.json`, `archive/`, `docs-backup/`, `.gitignore`, the extension's own state files): nothing.

A burst of 20 tool calls built the panel 146 times before this and 1–2 times after. The side bar's launcher counts only its badge while hidden. Moving the data out of the repo, with one change stamp in place of path routing, is #126.

### Panel redraw (#115)

1. **Input stamp.** `panel-stamp.js` `panelStamp` joins the full view, `db.changeStamp()`, the last database error, open documents' versions, the minute (for relative times) and a stat of the data folder and of the files under review. An equal stamp skips the page build: about 1.5 ms instead of 30–180 ms. It is not used on the Social and Task analyses tabs, which read other files, nor with every repo shown.
2. **Edits paging.** The Edits tab draws the newest 200 rows. "Show 500 more" and "Show all" ask the host for more (`view.rows`).
3. **Line diff.** The host keeps the lines it last sent and posts `{type: "diff", base, ver, ops}` (`line-diff.js`, Myers over the changed middle). The page applies the ops to its own copy with the same `applyOps`, inlined, and then draws through its usual update: nav, row patch, pane morph. A version the page does not have makes it post `resync`, and the host then sends the whole page. Edit rows carry ids counted from the oldest, and the hover previews are one JSON line per row, so a new row changes only its own lines.

Only the visible tab is drawn. A write by a plugin goes through the same change gate, so it is drawn like any other write.

#### Decisions settled

- 5575: live updates combine a leading-edge-plus-50ms local file watcher, a shared `PRAGMA data_version` change gate, a 500ms backstop poll while the panel is visible, a SQLite-backed Durable Object over WebSocket for cross-device push, and a signed GitHub webhook in place of the earlier 5-minute poll.

## 4. The panel as a board, with analytics (#147)

Epic #147, opened 2026-11-04. The Imprimatur panel looks and works like the ponytail board. The VS Code side bar stays as it is.

- **Board look on every tab (#148).** *Shipped in 0.95.0:* a near-black board palette, with a light variant on light themes. Cards have a soft gradient and an inner highlight, corners are rounder, and the app bar is translucent. High-contrast themes keep VS Code's colours, and text stays legible.
- **Session numbers (#149):** each Claude Code session's cost, time, lines and tokens.
- **One stats module (#150):** daily series, shared by the panel and `/imprimatur-stats`.
- **Board landing (#151):**
  - cards with sparklines;
  - a large chart with a metric switch and a 7d/30d/90d/All range;
  - a sessions table;
  - a 12-week activity heatmap with active days and streak.
- **Analytics on each tab (#152):** tasks over time, agent edits per day and the most edited files, document chapters filled, and hook cost.

<a id="the-whole-imprimatur-panel-becomes-a-board-in-th"></a>

## 5. The whole Imprimatur panel becomes a board in the ponytail board style, with session cost/time/tokens recorded and analytic views; the VS Code side bar stays

The user, on 2026-11-04, showing the ponytail board (`~/.config/ponytail/band/board.html`) beside the Imprimatur panel and side bar: "make it like the ponytail board. I do not want the views taken out of VS Code; the left pane can stay, but make this view like the ponytail board."

- Asked where the board look goes: "you will turn all of it into the board."
- Asked about cost: "yes, record it, and also good analytic views like the board."

What the user gets:

- **#148, the board look on every tab:** a near-black board palette with a light variant, cards with an inner highlight and a soft shadow, mono numbers, and a header with a breadcrumb and a range picker. The orange mascot and legible text stay, per the visual-style preference.
- **#149, session numbers:** each Claude Code session's cost, time and lines, from the status line input, and its tokens, from the transcript.
- **#150, one stats module:** daily series, shared by the panel and `/imprimatur-stats`.
- **#151, the board landing:** cards with sparklines, a large chart with a metric switch and a 7d/30d/90d/All range, a sessions table, and a 12-week activity heatmap with active days and streak.
- **#152, analytics on each tab:** tasks, agent changes, documents, and hook cost.

Not changed: the VS Code side bar (Imprimatur launcher, Agent setup).
